title: observability: token-level cost/latency dashboards + KV metrics + alert tuning
author: Priya Shah
body:
Summary:
This PR adds token-level cost and latency dashboards for inference routes, extends KV-cache instrumentation, and tunes alerts to reduce noisy paging during steady-state traffic. Motivation: customers and SREs need better per-token visibility (cost and latency split), and several incidents showed we lacked fine-grained KV-cache hit/miss and stall metrics.

What I changed (high level):
- New Grafana dashboard: observability/dashboards/token_cost_latency.json (route + model breakdowns, 95/99 latency slices, cost per-token by model family).
- KV cache metrics: pkg/metrics/token_kv_metrics.go adds kv_cache_hit_ratio, kv_stall_count, kv_stall_duration_ms (labels: route, model, shard).
- Tracing annotations: pkg/tracing/span_annotations.go now attaches token_count and kv_hit boolean to inference spans for downstream correlation.
- Alert rules: observability/alerts/token_latency.rules updated to add a two-tier alerting policy (warning at 95p > X, page at 99p > Y for >10m) and a KV stall rule that only pages when kv_stall_rate > threshold AND overall request error rate is elevated.
- Docs: docs/observability/alerting.md documents the new alert semantics and recommended runbooks.

Implementation notes:
- Metrics are exposed via the existing metrics registry; new metric names follow the redwood.<subsystem>.<metric> convention. Tag cardinality constrained to route/model/shard only to avoid high cardinality.
- Token cost is computed in the serving runtime by multiplying per-token compute units (from model profiles) with token counts emitted by the runtime; for hosted fallback we fallback to model-average cost.
- Dashboard panels include pre-aggregated PromQL expressions to keep dashboard performance acceptable.

Testing and validation:
- Unit tests added for new metric helpers and JSON schema for the dashboard file.
- Ran dashboard load test locally with synthetic traffic; dashboards render under 50ms for 7-day panels.
- Alert rules validated in staging for 48 hours; false-positive rate reduced by ~40% compared to prior rules.

Checklist:
- [x] Metrics added and exported
- [x] Dashboard JSON committed
- [x] Alert rules and runbook documented
- [x] Manual staging validation
- [x] Reviewed and approved by SREs

Migration/rollout:
- New metrics are additive; no migrations required. Alert changes will be rolled out to staging for 48h then to production on 2026-02-20.

Related: ENG-4821 (token-level observability epic), SUP-3342 (support ticket showing noisy pages during KV stalls).

review_comments: Alex Kim (2026-02-16): Left a couple of nits on metric naming. Can we make kv_stall_duration_ms a summary (histogram) instead of a gauge?
Priya Shah (2026-02-16): Thanks — switched kv_stall_duration_ms to a histogram and updated retention guidance in docs.
Marcus Li (2026-02-17): Alert tuning looks good. Request: add a suppression window for scheduled maintenance (we use label maintenance=true) — otherwise this will page during our backups.
Priya Shah (2026-02-17): Added suppression condition to the alert rule (maintenance label check).
Jordan Patel (2026-02-18): CI initially failed on dashboard schema lint (panel id duplication). I left a patch to dedupe IDs. After fix, re-ran CI and green.
Alex Kim (2026-02-19): Approved — left one optional suggestion to add a dashboard link from the route overview page.
